On the other hand, employees with a net income of not more than Four Hundred Fifty Thousand Pesos (P450,000.00) shall be given a twenty percent (20%) discount considring their ability to pay.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TOURISM since 2001-07-24

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING CERTAIN SECTIONS OF PRESIDENTIAL DECREE NO. 198, AS AMENDED AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES(re: Compensation Board of Directors of Provincial Water Utilities)
rows.abstract: This bill refers to the COMPENSATION Board of Directors of Provincial Water Utilities. The memo proposes THAT EACH DIRECTOR SHALL BE REIMBURSED HIS EXPENSES INCURRED IN CONNECTION WITH THE PERFORMANCE OF HIS FUNCTIONS IN SUCH AMOUNT AS MAY BE DETERMINED BY THE BOARD.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROMOTING VOLUNTARY BLOOD DONATION, PROVIDING FOR AN ADEQUATE SUPPLY OF SAFE BLOOD, REGULATING BLOOD BANKS AND PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF
rows.title_short: Promoting Voluntary Blood Donation, Providing for an Adequate Supply of Blood and Regulating Blood Banks
rows.abstract: This bill endorses the National Blood Services Program and encourages the establishment of blood collection centers in the country. Blood banks shall be establishd and operated according to professional and scientific standards and encouraged to beon a non-profit basis.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2001-07-24

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING PRIVATE AND PUBLIC SCHOOLS FROM DISALLOWING STUDENTS WITH DELINQUENT TUITION FEES TO TAKE THE MIDTERM OR FINAL EXAMINATIONS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: It is UNLAWFUL for any school, public or private, to disallow any student from taking any mid-term or final examination due to non-payment of tution fees not exceeding one installment under the established terms of payment described by the school concerned and approved by the Department of Education, Culture and Sports.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2001-07-24

rows.title_full: AN ACT DIRECTING THE DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION, CULTURE AND SPORTS TO INCLUDE IN THE CURRICULUM OF ALL ELEMENTARY AND SECONDARY SCHOOLS THE TEACHING OF RECYCLING AND COMPOSTING AS PART OF THE HEALTH SUBJECT
rows.abstract: Rationale: In proposing to integrate in the curriculum in the elementary and secondary levels within our educational system the teaching of recycling and composting, our main purpose is not simply to teach how to reduce, reuse and recycle. Through education, we hope to achieve a greater objective which is more to impart the correct values, proper attitude, right discipline, good training and the rigid, constant and consistent practice of good habits that are presumably instilled and ingrained in our daily life activities.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2001-07-24

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO INSTALL FAX MACHINE UNITS IN ALL CITIES AND MUNICIPALITIES THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract: Rationale: The bill proposes the installation of fax machine units in all cities and municipalities in the country to solve the communication barrier between the local governments and the National Government. With its implementation, it is expectedthat prompt and effective delivery of basic goods and services may be carried out and ultimately lead to the growth and prosperity even in obscure and distant cities and municipalities all over the country.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2001-07-24

rows.title_full: AN ACT DIRECTING THE DEPARTMENT OF EDUCATION, CULTURE AND SPORTS TO INCLUDE IN THE CURRICULUM OF ALL SECONDARY AND COLLEGIATE SCHOOLS AND UNIVERSITIES IN THE COUNTRY THE TEACHING OF POPULATION AND ENVIRONMENTAL DEVELOPMENT AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Population is a very broad subject indeed. Suffice it to say, with the fast deteriorating environment and rapid population growth in the country, it is but only timely to instill in the minds of our citizenry, specially the youth, the significance of POPULATION AND ENVIRONMENT DEVELOPMENT.
rows.status: Substituted by HR01097

rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE SOLAR ENERGY DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY, DEFINING ITS POWERS AND DUTIES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: We are currently experiencing some kind of an energy crisis-the prices of oil products are constantly rising.  We are too much dependent on imported crude oil for our energy, requirements which results in the diminution of out dollar reserves. > There are other souces of energy, like hydroelectric and geothermal energy, but the supply is inadequate. It is therefore, necessary that we explore and develop other alternative sources of enrgy like solar energy which is very abundant in our country.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ENERGY since 2001-07-24

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO ESTABLISH THE NATIONAL RECYCLING COMMISSION AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The proposed Commission is tasked principally to promote recycling and to take charge of solid wastes management and environmental sanitation.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ECOLOGY since 2001-07-24

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO ESTABLISH A NATIONAL JUNIOR POLICE AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The national junior police force shall assist the local officials, the regular police force, barangay officials and school officials in the implmentation of laws, ordinances and school regulations, in the maintenance of peace and order, in the dissemination of public information and in the performance of related duties as may de delegated by the chief executives of the local government units.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC ORDER AND SECURITY since 2001-07-24

rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING ALL PUBLIC UTILITY AGENCIES AND COMPANIES OR CORPORATIONS, BOTH PUBLIC AND PRIVATE, TO REPAIR ANY DIGGING OR DESTRUCTION MADE IN THE COURSE OF THEIR INSTALLATION OR MAINTENANCE WORK
rows.abstract: Any existing laws to the contrary notwithstanding , all public agencies, companies or corporations covered by this Act shall, within seventy two (72) hours from completion of any work affecting any road, street passageway, pathway and similar places, repair or reconstruct the same by restoring it to its status prior to such work. The repair or reconstruction shall be done in the presence of the punong barangay concerned, or in his absence, the barangay secretary, who is hereby required to issuea certificate of repair work completion. A copy of the certificate shall be retained by the barangay official for barangay record purposes.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC WORKS AND HIGHWAYS since 2001-07-24

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO REQUIRE THE TEACHING OF BASIC COMPUTER PROGRAMMING AS PART OF THE CURRICULUM OF ALL SECONDARY SCHOOLS IN THE COUNTRY AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: We are living in the Age of Modern Technology and Information wherein computers have become a part of almost every field of human endeavor. Computers have proven to be necessary and useful to most organization and business corporations because these have made human work easier, faster and more efficient. As a whole, computers have generally improved the quality of life of man.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2001-07-24

rows.author: C103
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A CRISIS AND REHABILITATION CENTER FOR VICTIMS OF SEXUAL ABUSE
rows.abstract: Rationale: Victims of sexual abuses need more help from professionals and experts to contain the trauma they suffered. Campaigns and mass eduction have to be implemented to raise the awareness of the people and involve the community in the prevention and treatment of victims of rape and other sexually related abuse. Social workers, psychologists, psychiatrists, and other medical professionals have to be mobilized in the rehabilitation of victims and importantly in the prevention of sexual abuses committed against women.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WOMEN since 2001-07-24

rows.author: C103
rows.title_full: AN ACT EXPANDING THE COVERAGE OF SCHOOLS OF THE SCHOLARSHIP FUND FOR POOR BUT DESERVING STUDENTS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: The Local Government Code is proposed to be amended as follows: Establish a scholarship fund for poor but deserving students residing within the muncipality in (schools located within its jurisdiction), OR CITY, AS THE CASE MAY BE, IN SCHOOLS WITHINTHE PROVINCE."
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2001-07-24

rows.author: C103
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROMOTING PUBLIC PARTICIPATION IN PUBLIC UTILITIES AND PROHIBITING THE IMPOSITION OF COMPULSORY INVESTMENTS TO THE PUBLIC
rows.abstract: This measure aims to truly democratize the ownership of public utilities by promoting popular participation and prohibiting the imposition of any compulsory investments in such utilities.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRADE AND INDUSTRY since 2001-07-24

rows.author: C103
rows.title_full: AN ACT TRANSFERRING THE POWERS AND FUNCTIONS OF THE OFFICE OF THE GOVERNMENT CORPORATE COUNSEL (OGCC) TO THE OFFICE OF THE SOLICITOR GENERAL (OSG)
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to ABOLISH the Office of the Government Corporate Counsel (OGCC). Rationale: This Act will minimize the unnecessary duplication and overlapping of agency functions. The transfer of powers and functions by the OGCC to the OSG, will lead to a more efficient execution of functions and at the same time it will generate budgetary savings which can be utilized to implement other priority projects and programs of the government.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2001-07-24

rows.status: Substituted by HB04686

rows.title_full: AN ACT MANDATING THE ESTABLISHMENT OF MUNICIPAL LIBRARIES IN THE ONE THOUSAND FIVE HUNDRED FORTY-THREE MUNICIPALITIES NATIONWIDE
rows.abstract: This bill aims to give as many children as possible the chance to develop their potential. It would be a pity if the talent in a child which would flower if tended should be left to wither because the child has no access to informative reading materials. This bill hopes to see all children grow to the apex of their capabilities.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2001-07-24

rows.title_full: AN ACT INCREASING THE MONTHLY PENSION OF FILIPINO WAR VETERANS AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: The monthly pension of all Filipino War Veterans is hereby increased by FIFTY PER CENTUM (50%).
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on  since 2001-07-24

rows.title_full: AN ACT CHANGING THE SCHOOL CALENDAR FROM JUNE THROUGH MARCH TO SEPTEMBER THROUGH MAY
rows.abstract: Rationale: The existing school calendar which is yearly scheduled from June through March is no longer suited for the students today, particularly in Central Luzon wherein lahar avalanche spawned by Mt. Pinatubo continue to plague the region, specially during the rainy season. > This bill seeks to CHANGE the school calendar from June through March to September through May.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2001-07-24

rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING MANPOWER AND LIVELIHOOD TRAINING CENTERS IN ALL MUNICIPALITIES AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREOF
rows.abstract: This bill proposes to bring education to the grassroots level by creating manpower and livelihood training centers in all municipalities nationwide. In facing the challenges of this "technological era," the quality of a country's labor force and thesize of its technical manpower stock are essential. Productivity growth which arises through successful technology transfer requires workers that have a level of training and a mix of skills appropriate for the needs of the industry, agriculture, and service sector.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2001-07-24

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING THE ESTABLISHMENT OF POLITICAL DYNASTIES
rows.abstract: Rationale: It is the policy of the State to guarnatee equal access of opportunities to public office and to democratize the exercise of political power. Towards this end, the state shall PROHIBIT the establishment of political dynasties.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SUFFRAGE AND ELECTORAL REFORMS since 2001-07-24

rows.title_full: AN ACT ACCORDING BIRTHDAY LEAVE BENEFITS OF ONE (1) DAY WITH PAY TO ALL EMPLOYEES IN THE PRIVATE AND PUBLIC SECTORS AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: All employees in the private and public sectors shall be entitled to a birthday leave of one (1) day with pay on his/her natal dayl falling on a regular working day.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2001-07-24

rows.title_full: AN ACT DEFINING AND PENALIZING THE CRIMES OF LOOTING, STEALING FROM, AND DESECRATING THE VICTIMS DURING AND IN THE AFTERMATH OF  NATURAL OR MANMADE CALAMITIES AND ACCIDENTS AND PRESCRIBING PENALTIES THEREFOR
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to classify as heinous crime all acts of looting, stealing from and desecrating the bodies of victims during or in the aftermath of natural or man-made calamities and accidents and providing penalties therefor.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2001-07-24

ACCORDINGLY, THE STATE SHALL MAINTAIN A PROFESSIONAL AND RESPONSIVE CAREER FOREIGN SERVICE.

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO AMEND REPUBLIC ACT NO. 8239, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE PHILIPPINE PASSPORT ACT OF 1996
rows.title_short: Amending RA 8239, Otherwise Known as the Philippine Passport Act of 1996
rows.abstract: Specifically, this bill seeks to amend the provisions relating to the requirements for issuance of passports as well as additional grounds for its amendment, suspension and revocation. Furthermore, the proposed bill enumerates the individuals who shall be qualified to file applications on bahalf of certain applicants in specific circumstances provided therein.> Finally, the bill also seeks to penalize those who do damage to the Philippine passport's integrity and validity by punishing those whoshall sell passport applications, government forms, as well as lost or stolen documents.
rows.status: Approved by the House on 2001-12-19, transmitted to on 2002-01-02 and received by the Senate on 2002-01-02

second_reading.remarks: Considered the Explanatory Notes of the original HB Nos. 745 and 1241 as sponsorship remarks.

rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE PARAMETERS OF ECONOMIC, SOCIAL AND CULTURAL RELATIONS BETWEEN THE PEOPLE OF THE PHILIPPINES AND THE PEOPLE OF TAIWAN
rows.abstract: Rationale: In view of the adoption of the Philippines of its one-China policy pursuant to the Joint Communique dated June 9, 1975 between the Republic of the Philippines and the People's Republic of China and the absence of formal diplomatic relations with the authorities on Taiwan, Congress finds it necessary to establish the parameters for a closer and more active interaction between the people of the Philippines and the people on Taiwan in the areas of economics, trade, commercial, cultural,social and othr mutually beneficial relations.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04962

rows.author: C076
rows.title_full: AN ACT AUTHORIZING THE TRANSFER OF SENTENCED PERSONS TO OR FROM FOREIGN COUNTRIES
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to authorize the Secretary of Justice to receive the custody of a Filipino sentenced abroad or cause the transfer of an alien serving sentence in Philippine penitentiaries in accordance with the provisions of the transfer of sentenced persons treaties between the Philippines and another country. It provides for a procedure in securing the consent of sentenced persons and the verification of such consent. It also provides for the administrative costs attendant to the transfer ofsentenced Filipino prisoners.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on FOREIGN AFFAIRS since 2001-07-24

rows.author: C076
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE PHILIPPINE DRUG ENFORCEMENT ADMINISTRATION DEFINING ITS POWER AND FUNCTIONS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: An agency is hereby created to be known as the "Philippine Drug Enforcement Administration" , hereinafter referred to as PDEA, which be shall responsible for the efficient and effective enforcement of all laws on prohibited and regulated drugs and other controlled substances.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on DANGEROUS DRUGS since 2001-07-24

first_reading.comm_act: ch. of cttee. ref'l from Gov't Reorg. as per J.35; p.41

rows.author: C076
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO PROVIDE MAXIMUM EMPLOYMENT IN PUBLIC ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT PROJECTS, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: In order to provide employment opportunities around the country, the Legislative ad Executive Departments shall jointly formulate a public employment program. However, to ensure that all districts and sectors shall benefit for the public employmentprogram, the identificaiton of the projects shall be determined by the members of the House of Representatives , and its execution shall be in coordination with the government agency concerned. Members of the Senate shall also propose their own employment programs and executed in coordination with the government agency concerned in furtherance of the objectives of this Act.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2001-07-24

rows.author: C076
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING CERTAIN PROVISIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7202, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE SUGAR RESTITUTION LAW AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: It has been six years since the enabling of the Sugar Restitution Act. Yet to the continued frustration of what remains of the sugar industry today, no actual and tangible recource has been made available to anyone. It is against this backdrop the amendments to R.A. 7202 are herein proposed to provide teeth and easy accountability towards its quick and full implementation. > Section 2 of R.A. 7202 shall be amended to include a specific procedure in the sourcing and allotments of funds as well as to outline incentives towads paradigm shifting to consider alternative high-value crops.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05304

rows.author: C076
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2003-12-17, transmitted to on 2003-12-18 and received by the Senate on 2004-01-06
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING THE PHILIPPINE COAST GUARD AS A SEPARATE AND DISTINCT SERVICE ATTACHED TO THE DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION AND COMMUNICATIONS, FURTHER AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 5173 AS AMENDED AND FOR THE OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: To effect the original intent of the Philippine Coast Guard, there is a need to amend Republic Act No. 5173 to separate the PCG from the PN (Philippine Navy) and attach the same to the Department of Transporttion and Communications (DOTC). The proposed transfer will achieve the original intentions of having a unified and integrated approach to the country's maritime safety and water transport development programs. It seeks to complement earlier safety and water transport developmentpograms. It seeks to complement earlier efforts under Executive Order 477 s. 1998 which transferred to the Philippine Coast Guard to the Department of Transportation and Communications. Indeed, with this proposed bill, the PCG would be able to fullyconcentrate on its functions toward Maritime Safety Administration, Marine Environmental Protection, Maritime Search and Rescue and Marine Law Enforcement.
rows.status: Substituted by HB06478

rows.author: C076
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 90, PERTAINING TO THE PRACTICE OF PROFESSION, OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991(LOCAL OFFICIALS'PRACT ICE OF PROFESSION)
rows.abstract: Rationale: Many of these elective local government officials are compelled to give-up their lucrative practice of profession to their personal detriment. On the other hand, it is still possible to allow them a limited practice of their profession that will not be detrimental to their functions as local government officials. This bill seeks to carve out that middle ground by distinguishing among the different local goverment officials and defining to what extent they may practice their profession.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2001-07-24

rows.author: C076
rows.title_full: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A "JOB ASSISTANCE AND LIVELIHOOD PROGRAM" IN THE MUNICIPALITIES OF THE FIFTH DISTRICT OF NEGROS OCCIDENTAL, PROVIDING INCENTIVES AND FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2001-07-24

rows.author: C095
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A COMPREHENSIVE WATER QUALITY MANAGEMENT POLICY AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Clean Water is one of the most basic necessities of life. However, as we approach the next millennium, nature's filter system cannot recycle and generate clean water as fast as necessary to sustain and preserve life. There is an urgent need to enact a law that will provide a framework of policies that will help ensure that our entire water system is rehabilitated, protected and allowed to regenerate clean water. This bill, therefore, seeks to provide for a comprehensive water qualitymanagement policy to addres this critical need.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05398

rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TOURISM since 2001-07-24

rows.author: B004
rows.title_full: mN ACT ADDRESSING THE SYSTEM OF PROSTITUTION, IMPOSING PENALTIES ON ITS PERPETRATORS, PROVIDING PROTECTIVE MEASURES AND SUPPORT SERVICES FOR ITS VICTIMS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE THE REVISED PENAL CODE, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Prostitution must be approached in its entirety, interrogating both the structural mechanism and the ideological justifications which uphold it. In addressing prostitution, the Government must address the contradictions in policies which, in effect,reinforce the system of prostitution. The adult-child divide must be removed and women and children in prostitution must be decriminalized alike. The goal of minimizing if not totally eradicting prostitution, must be directed against establishmentsand male customers who control and profit from the business of prostitution. Policies and programs must be developed that will address the problems of women in prostitution, provide them protection, penalize those who control, perpetuate, and benefitt from the business of prostitution, address the factors in general that perpetuate prostitution, and serve to eradicate prostitution in the long term.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2001-07-24

rows.abstract: Disabled persons are as vulnerable as the senior citizens. They should be given the same privileges enjoyed by senior citizens. This would surely boost morale of the disabled. And make them feel that they are still a member of the society with lessburden to their families.

rows.author: C017
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING CERTAIN SECTIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NUMBERED SEVENTY-EIGHT HUNDRED AND THIRTY-SIX, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS "THE PHILIPPINE TEACHERS PROFESSIONALIZA TION ACT OF 1994"
rows.abstract: This legislative initiative proposes to amend Section 22 and Section 26 of R.A. No. 7836 otherwise known and cited as "The Philippine Teachers Professionaliza tion Act of 1994." The proposed amendment for the Section 22 calls for the automatic and mandatory membership of professional teachers into an integrated national organization recognized and accredited by the National Teachers Board and the Professional Regulations Commission. While the proposed amendment to Section 26 extends the prescriptive registation period for qualified teachers to register with the Board up to December 31. 2003.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05411

The Clark International Airport,  with its existing runways and airport area of Two Thousand Two Hundred (2,200) hectares provides sufficient area for phased expansion to serve the air traffic demand of the 21st Century.
